title: Present Value Basics
description: Introduction to time value of money and present value concepts.
html:
The time value of money

A dollar today is generally worth more than a dollar received in the future because today's dollar can potentially be invested and earn a return.

Two important ideas

Future Value: What money today could grow to in the future.

Present Value: What a future amount of money is worth today.

Simple future value example

Suppose you invest $1,000 for one year at 10%.

$1,000 × 1.10 = $1,100

The future value after one year is $1,100.

Now work backward

If someone promises to pay you $1,100 one year from now and the appropriate discount rate is 10%, its present value is:

$1,100 ÷ 1.10 = $1,000

Basic present value formula

PV = FV ÷ (1 + r)ⁿ

PV = Present Value

FV = Future Value

r = Interest or discount rate

n = Number of periods

Accounting connection

Present value concepts become important later when you study topics such as bonds, leases and certain long-term obligations.

Example

You will receive $10,000 one year from now. Assume a 5% discount rate.

Present Value = $10,000 ÷ 1.05

Present Value ≈ $9,523.81

Don't overcomplicate this yet

At this stage, the goal is simply to understand why future cash flows may be worth less today.

We'll do much more detailed present-value calculations when we reach bonds and leases.

quiz.prompt: What is the present value of $1,100 received one year from now if the discount rate is 10%?

objectives: Explain present value basics and its underlying principles.
Apply the topic to a financial-reporting scenario.
